films.title: Where You Been?
films.description: Harry Reynolds' 27-minute Uprise Skateshop full-length follows 31 skaters through Chicago and the wider Midwest street landscape. Three years in the making, the film preserves the complete first-party order of appearance and credits 13 additional camera contributors.
creditNotes: Uprise Skateshop's authorized complete-film description names all 31 skaters in order of appearance, credits Harry Reynolds for filming and editing and lists 13 additional filmers.

TransWorld independently calls the work a full-length, repeats the complete 31-skater lineup and corroborates the three-year Chicago production; SkateVideoSite independently classifies it as a 27-minute 2026 shop film and catalogs the same riders and camera contributors.

The first-party spelling is retained where sources differ: Billy Dusczynski, Dylan Lulloff, Gerardo Mendoza, Kevin Kuszcowski and Oliver Placencia-Chermansky. No unsupported solo-part hierarchy is assigned from the order-of-appearance list.
films.locationNote: Uprise, TransWorld, Quartersnacks and SkateVideoSite all identify Chicago as the film's center; TransWorld describes the wider setting only as Chicago and beyond, so no unsupported additional city is added.
films.historicalContext: Three years in the making, Where You Been? is Uprise's contemporary Chicago shop full-length and a document of Midwest street skating, with crust, difficult weather and a deep local crew foregrounded in contemporary coverage.
films.artworkNotes: The exact authorized upload's 1280x720 YouTube artwork and player were visually reviewed on 2026-09-18. The black title card with the handwritten Where you been? lettering is dedicated film artwork, and the page carries no trailer, episode or compilation labeling.

films.title: JHAKX VIDEO 2
films.description: Yuuki Morishita's 20-minute second JHAKX video links New York, Los Angeles, San Francisco, Tokyo and Osaka through five city chapters filmed from 2023 to 2026. The first-party credits contain 51 unique rider labels, including one unresolved Big-T credit, while the independent filmography identifies 50 named skaters and expands the Buckets and Lurker Lou aliases.
creditNotes: JHAKX Skateboards' authorized complete-film description groups the credited appearances into New York, Los Angeles, San Francisco, Tokyo and Osaka chapters and formally credits Yuuki Morishita for filming and editing.

Skate Jawn independently calls it the second JHAKX video, identifies Morishita and all five cities and names a representative cast; SkateVideoSite independently classifies it as a 20-minute 2026 work and catalogs 50 named skaters.

The first-party description lists 52 city-chapter entries: Ty Beall appears in both New York and Tokyo, leaving 51 unique labels. SkateVideoSite normalizes 50 people and omits Big-T; TrickBook preserves Big-T as an unresolved first-party rider label without inventing an identity, while expanding Buckets and Lurker Lou from independent corroboration.
locations: New York City, New York, United States
films.locationNote: The official film description and Skate Jawn both identify all five city chapters; SkateVideoSite independently corroborates each city and the United States/Japan scope.
films.historicalContext: The second JHAKX video turns footage gathered from 2023 through 2026 into a trans-Pacific five-city project, connecting three major United States street-skating centers with Tokyo and Osaka.
films.artworkNotes: The exact authorized upload's 1280x720 YouTube artwork and player were visually reviewed on 2026-09-18. The action frame carries the central JHAKX Skate Boards Inc. mark and is the official complete-film image; the page carries no trailer or episodic labeling.
